When it slips and nobody tells them, the promise breaks, and a support ticket is how they let you know. Proactive shipping notifications either keep the promise or keep the shopper posted. Key takeaways 70% of shoppers say an accurate delivery date at checkout is very important, the highest-rated factor in Narvar's 2026 holiday research. 65% of shoppers feel anxious about the season. A date that changes without warning is where that anxiety turns into a ticket. Notify's predictive delay emails measure every delay against the date you promised, so the shopper hears the new date from you first. A gift, a date, and a tracking page Picture a shopper who orders a gift in mid-December because your site promised it would arrive before the holiday. Two days before that date, they refresh the tracking page and see a new delivery date. Nobody told them. They aren't thinking about carriers or scan events. They're thinking the gift will be late, and that you didn't say so. Their next move is your support inbox. Care teams log that message as WISMO. For the shopper, it's a question about whether they can count on you, and this year that question carries more weight. 70% of shoppers say an accurate delivery date at checkout is very important when making a holiday purchase, the highest-rated factor in our entire consumer survey. - Delivering the 2026 Holiday Shopping Season The same research found that 65% of shoppers feel anxious about the season , so they're watching that date closely. And dates do move: 37% of shoppers saw the delivery date change after they bought last peak. And a promise that slips does more damage than no promise at all. Want the full shopper data for 2026 Peak? See what 1,348 consumers say is important to them this holiday shopping season. Download the report . ‍ The four questions behind the ticket Between "shipped" and "delivered," a shopper's worry takes four forms. Here's what they hear from you today, and what a proactive message tells them instead. "Is it still coming on time?" This is the question your promise creates. When the date changes and nobody says so, the shopper finds out from a tracking page or from an empty doorstep. A carrier delay email waits for the carrier to report a problem. A Notify predictive delay email works from Narvar's own prediction, built from carrier and order data, and compares it with the date you promised at checkout. The promise was yours, so the update comes from you, before the shopper goes looking. "Did I miss it?" The carrier tried, nobody was home, and a slip on the door is the only explanation. The shopper can't tell if the parcel is back at the depot or coming tomorrow. An attempted delivery or exception email tells them what happened and what comes next, in your brand's voice instead of the carrier's. "Is it even moving?" Nothing has gone wrong. The parcel is on schedule. But between "shipped" and "delivered" the shopper hears nothing, and a gift with a deadline turns every quiet day into doubt. A delivery-anticipation email goes out about 24 hours before arrival. It replaces the silence with the one fact the shopper wants: your order arrives tomorrow. "It says delivered. So where is it?" No email makes a missing parcel appear. But a shopper who has heard from you at every step before this one starts the conversation expecting you to help, not bracing for a runaround. This is also the ticket your care team should plan for. Pull this report before you hire holiday helpdesk temps and show them how to size it. Keep the promise or keep them posted Retailers and shoppers already agree on one thing: the holiday research found both sides favor resolving delivery problems proactively, before they turn into a support issue . The retailers who act on it see the difference. Once Davines could reach shoppers proactively during shipping and fulfillment delays, its WISMO inquiries fell 22% within a few weeks. At Molton Brown , WISMO dropped out of the top 10 contact drivers entirely within three months. Narvar calls this brand hospitality: how cared for a shopper feels in every moment after the sale. A shopper who hears about a delay from you, in your voice, has been taken care of. That's the shopper who comes back in January. Your shoppers will have questions this December. It's up to you if they hear the answer from you first. The data you need to reduce WISMO tickets is already in your helpdesk, and acting on it before December means fewer contacts now and more repeat buyers in January. Key takeaways Last holiday season, 37% of US shoppers had a package arrive late, and 37% saw the delivery date change after they ordered. Your helpdesk already holds your peak WISMO count. Pull it, cost it at about $12 a contact, and sort it by cause before you finalize temp headcount. Shipped and delivered emails miss the moments that create tickets. But predictive delay, exception, and delivery-anticipation emails cover them. The payoff runs past cost: 44% of shoppers say order and delivery notifications would make them buy from you again. The number missing from your staffing plan Care teams are signing off on holiday temps right now. Before you sign yours, check one figure: how many of last peak's tickets were shoppers asking where their order was? The fastest way to reduce those WISMO tickets is to answer the question before the shopper asks it, and the four steps below show you how. In our recent holiday report , we surveyed 1,348 US shoppers and 100 retailers, and it shows where those tickets begin: 37% of shoppers had a package arrive late last peak; 37% watched the delivery date change after purchase; and 23% had a package marked delivered that never arrived. Every one of those problems starts after the order ships, when a shopper's only line to you is a tracking page or your support inbox. Both sides feel it: 68% of shoppers rate on-time delivery "very important," and 66% of retailers rank it a top-three peak challenge. Want the full shopper data for 2026 Peak? See what 1,348 consumers say is important to them this holiday shopping season. Download the report . Run the audit in an afternoon The four steps below turn last peak's ticket history into a number you can plan around. The first two tell you how many WISMO tickets you had and what they cost. The last two show which of those tickets a tool like Narvar Notify can prevent, and how to handle the ones that still come in. 1. Pull last November and December from your helpdesk Filter Zendesk, Kustomer, or Gorgias to last year's peak and pull every ticket tagged order status, shipping, or delivery. If tagging differs across teams, search subject lines and first messages for "where is," "hasn't arrived," "tracking," and "says delivered." Running several brands or regions? Split the pull by each one, because the split tells you which brand or market to fix first. Record three figures: total WISMO tickets, their share of all peak tickets, and your busiest week. 2. Put a dollar figure on it Each call-center contact can cost from $3 to $12. Multiply your team's contact cost by your WISMO count and you have last peak's handling cost for a single question. Then take your busiest week and divide it by what one temp agent clears in a week. That’s how many of this year's temps you are hiring to read tracking pages back to shoppers. 3. Match each cause to its fix The tickets in your pull trace back to moments your current emails skip. Shopify and most commerce platforms send two messages, shipped and delivered, and neither one arrives when a shopper starts to worry. Start with the biggest bucket: late parcels and moved dates. A Notify predictive delay alert covers both, telling the shopper the new date before they notice the old one has slipped. Next, pull out missed and stuck deliveries. An attempted delivery or exception email explains what happened and what comes next, so the shopper doesn't have to ask. The last bucket is the one you might overlook: orders where nothing went wrong, but the shopper heard nothing between "shipped" and "delivered." A delivery-anticipation email, sent about 24 hours before arrival, fills that gap. Shoppers open these messages because each one answers the question they were about to send you. Predictive delay emails average 38% click-through and attempted delivery emails 34%. A delivered email averages 8%. The one message your platform already sends is the one shoppers are most likely to skip. 4. Answer the rest inside the ticket Some tickets will still arrive, including the "it says delivered, but it isn't here" contact. On Zendesk, the Narvar Connect + Care app gives agents the order, its shipping status, and notification history, inside the ticket. Agents resend an email from the same screen, without switching to another tool. How many temps are you hiring to read tracking pages back to shoppers? What this looks like across 80+ brands An audit tells you where your tickets come from. These retailers show what happens once you start answering shoppers first, from a portfolio of more than 80 brands to a single-brand UK retailer. Newell Brands runs Notify across more than 80 brands and averages a 20% reduction in WISMO. Fortnum & Mason , the London gifting retailer, cut WISMO queries by 50% with Narvar order data inside its Zendesk workflow. Hibbett Sports brought contacts per order down by more than 20%. Fewer tickets, more repeat buyers 44% of shoppers say order and delivery notifications would make them buy from a retailer again. ‍ - Delivering the 2026 Holiday Shopping Season A shopper who hears about a delay from you, before checking a tracking page, has no reason to open a ticket. They also have a reason to trust you with the next order. For example, since Clarins started using Notify, its customers are 3x more likely to repurchase. That turns your WISMO count into a loyalty metric. The same message that keeps a ticket out of your December queue brings the shopper back in January. blogs.content: Hanukkah Campaign Ideas for Q4 Generated by Klaviyo AI The article outlines eight ways brands can create relevant Hanukkah campaigns while respecting the holiday’s traditions. It covers AI search visibility, audience segmentation, gift recommendations, recipes, reviews, giveaways, and seasonal products. Improve gift discovery: Use specific product descriptions, gifting FAQs, organized gift guides, and detailed reviews to improve visibility in AI searches. Target relevant audiences: Build segments from past Hanukkah purchases, campaign engagement, browsing behavior, and cart activity. Test seasonal campaigns: Use AI-assisted campaign creation to test messaging, imagery, timing, and channel combinations. Offer useful content: Share gift recommendations and recipes tailored to customers’ preferences and purchase histories. Build future relevance: Collect holiday-themed reviews and promote seasonal products to generate data for future campaigns. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights, is a Jewish celebration of resilience and tradition. Rooted in a miracle in which oil lit a lamp for 8 days even though it was only enough for one, it’s a time for family gatherings, lighting the menorah, and indulging in treats like sufganiyot and latkes. Gift giving is a more recent addition to Hanukkah traditions. Gelt , small amounts of money given to Torah teachers and students, has been part of the holiday since the 1600s in Eastern Europe, but wrapped presents didn't become common until the mid-20th century. This is when American Jewish families started giving gifts alongside the older custom of gelt, largely in response to the popularity of gift giving at Christmas . In 2026, Hanukkah begins at sundown on Friday, December 4 and ends at nightfall on Saturday, December 12. Hanukkah always starts on the 25th day of the Hebrew month of Kislev. Because the Jewish calendar is lunisolar, the dates shift annually, typically falling anywhere between late November and late December. As a holiday that’s about much more than presents, Hanukkah is an opportunity for brands to engage with customers in a way that honors these traditions while also providing unique value. Whether it’s highlighting exclusive products, offering a Hanukkah-themed gift guide, or creating campaigns centered around family, tradition, and the spirit of the season, there are plenty of ways to show your customers that your brand understands and respects the essence of Hanukkah. Here are 8 Hanukkah marketing ideas, one for each candle on the menorah: 1. Show up in gift-related AI searches Consumers are actively searching for the perfect gifts for their loved ones during the holidays. According to Klaviyo's 2026 State of the Holiday Buyer Report , 67% of consumers say they already have a gift idea in mind before they start shopping. When they do that, they’ll see a higher variety of product options on Google than they will with an LLM. But according to the same report, 1 in 4 shoppers are using AI to get personalized gift ideas or recommendations. This means you’ll want your brand to show up in those AI search results, too. Here are a few ways to improve your brand's chances of showing up in AI shopping searches: Write product descriptions like you're answering a question. Rather than describing a product as a "wool blend scarf," try "a soft, wool blend scarf that keeps you warm on milder winter nights, in sizes to fit teens through adults." The more specific the use case, the more likely LLMs are to surface your product for a query like, "I need a cozy gift for grandma." Add FAQs that answer real Hanukkah gifting questions. Go beyond sizing and shipping. Answer questions like, "Is this a good gift for someone's first Hanukkah?" or, "Can this be personalized for a bar or bat mitzvah, too?" This gives LLMs full context to pull from for deeper queries. Build gift guides organized by who people are shopping for. A Hanukkah gift guide for coworkers under $30, for example, gives LLMs a direct match for how people actually search. Ask for reviews that mention gifting. Use custom review questions to prompt customers to leave more specific reviews, so LLMs can feature them in comparison guides and make life easier for shoppers when they’re considering multiple products. Hanukkah marketing example: ModernTribe structures their gift guide with specifics ModernTribe , a Judaica and Jewish gifts retailer, structures their Hanukkah gift guide in a way that's built to be found in AI search results. Rather than one Hanukkah gift category, the page categorizes products into smaller collections like Hanukkah decorations, Hanukkah candles for sale, and Hanukkah clothes: the same kind of natural language phrasing a shopper might type into ChatGPT or Gemini when asking for gift ideas. ModernTribe Hanukkah marketing tip: The page also updates throughout the season and includes a real-time social proof pop-up showing recent purchases from other shoppers. Signals like these help both shoppers and LLMs contextualize the product recommendations. 2. Grow your subscriber lists with a Hanukkah contest or giveaway Hanukkah's 8 nights give you a way to engage multiple segments of your audience on the channels they most want to engage with. For example, you may have email subscribers who would rather interact with you via text message, but they don’t know they can. Or you may have Instagram followers who don’t know they could get exclusive perks and early access if they sign up for emails, text messages, or WhatsApp. Consider launching an Instagram giveaway that asks your followers to subscribe via DM for a chance to enter. You can also ask them to tag a friend who doesn’t follow you yet, or tag you in a post of them using your product. Marketing example: Thirdlove offers a giveaway to grow their Instagram following Intimates brand Thirdlove ran an Instagram giveaway for a $300 gift certificate that required entrants to follow Thirdlove on social media, like the post, and tag a friend in a comment. Thirdlove Instagram Hanukkah marketing tip: Consider giving away a product tied to Hanukkah to make your promotion seasonally appropriate. That could mean a limited-edition item in Hanukkah's traditional blue and white, a bundle of 8 items, or a food and drink gift box built for a Hanukkah gathering. Or, partner with an aligned brand to sweeten the deal and increase your reach. Once you have people who are subscribed to multiple marketing channels, you can use AI-powered channel affinity to determine which channels they’re most likely to engage with next. 3. Use vibe marketing to test Hanukkah promotions Vibe marketing is AI prompt-based campaign creation that works with your data, brand guidelines, and other guardrails to create emails and text messages. Ask your AI marketing agent to help you bring your Hanukkah marketing campaigns to life with these example prompts: "Build a Hanukkah email that announces a one-night-only discount on the first night of the holiday, and segment it so VIP customers get early access." "Write 3 versions of a Hanukkah text message: one that uses humor, one that leans nostalgic and family-focused, and one that's straightforward and deal-driven, so I can test which tone performs best." "Build an omnichannel flow that sends a Hanukkah gift guide email 30 days before the holiday, follows up with a text message reminder a week later for anyone who hasn't opened it, and closes with a final text 5 days before Hanukkah for last-minute shoppers, timed to when and where each subscriber is most likely to engage." Hanukkah marketing example: GourmetGiftBaskets.com shares their holiday bundle Artisanal gift basket brand GourmetGiftBaskets.com , known for baskets packed with fresh fruit, fine wine, baked goods, and more, shares a themed gift basket in this Hanukkah marketing example. blogs.content: Use AI agents to scale BFCM service Generated by Klaviyo AI The article explains how K:AI Customer Agent, an AI shopping assistant within Klaviyo’s autonomous B2C CRM, supports customers during Black Friday Cyber Monday. It covers use cases from personalized recommendations and cart nudges to order management and omnichannel support, highlighting how AI reduces support load while maintaining fast, consistent service. Personalized recommendations: Customer Agent uses customer and product data to deliver tailored product suggestions, comparisons, and sizing guidance that feel more human than basic chatbots and can increase BFCM revenue. Omnichannel assistance: By operating across web chat, SMS, email, RCS, and soon WhatsApp, Customer Agent keeps conversations connected so shoppers receive consistent help wherever they interact with a brand. Cart and checkout nudges: Real-time answers to common questions, in-conversation “add to cart” prompts, and guidance during browsing help reduce abandonment caused by slow responses or confusing checkout flows. Automated order support: Customer Agent resolves routine inquiries about shipping status, returns, exchanges, and delivery issues, freeing human agents to focus on high-value customers during peak BFCM volume. Seamless human handoff: When issues are too complex, Customer Agent routes conversations to Klaviyo Helpdesk with full context, allowing human agents to step in quickly without forcing customers to repeat information. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary AI shopping assistants are changing the way people shop during Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM). Over the past couple of years, Amazon rolled out Rufus, an AI shopping assistant for customers, and other large brands have followed suit. Consumers are quickly adopting the technology, too: 78% have used AI shopping tools, according to Klaviyo’s 2025 AI consumer shopping survey . People want speed and value—and at no time is this more true than during BFCM . To meet high-volume demand during BFCM, AI shopping assistants, or customer agents, can help busy marketing and customer service teams deliver quick, personalized service and shopping experiences. Klaviyo is the autonomous B2C CRM, and K:AI Customer Agent was built to talk to your customers. It answers common questions, makes personalized recommendations, and nudges people to finish a purchase after they abandon a cart, all of which drive BFCM sales. Here are a few ways you can use Customer Agent to improve the customer experience and keep up with demand, no matter how busy you get during BFCM. 1. Make personalized recommendations with an AI shopping assistant A million-plus orders an hour also means a million-plus chances to recommend the right next product, and no team can do that by hand in real time. Customer Agent helps your team sell faster during that rush because it's trained on your customer data and your storefront. When it can see personal preferences, on-site behavior, and buying-intent signals, it skips the generic, robotic replies people have come to expect from a basic chatbot. Let’s say a BFCM shopper comes across a social media campaign for an arts supply brand and decides to visit their ecommerce store. While searching for paints, brushes, and canvases, the shopper compares deals across multiple tabs. They zero in on a beginner painter’s bundle, but they need to make sure it’s age-appropriate for their 8-year-old niece. Customer Agent delivers a precise answer and, within the brief exchange, learns that the shopper is buying a gift for a young artist. Just before check-out, the AI agent up-sells the customer on a deal for an easel—a must-have for newbies. Here are just a few more examples of how Customer Agent can use your data to offer more informed, relevant recommendations that are more likely to increase revenue: Recommending products based on a specific query: When a shopper asks a specific question, Customer Agent can then send them product recommendations related to their question. Providing personal BFCM shopping assistance: BFCM incentivizes customers to search widely for the best deals. Conversational assistance such as product comparisons or sizing guidance can keep visitors engaged and ultimately close more sales by speeding up the consideration stage. The bottom line: Personalized attention can make each shopper feel like they’re your only customer. An AI shopping assistant trained on your customer and product data gives more detailed, relevant recommendations, and it can grow revenue without pulling in a human. 2. Add Customer Agent to the channels where your customers already are BFCM shoppers don’t stick to one channel—they move between your website, text messages, and inbox throughout their buying journey. By adding Customer Agent to each of these touchpoints, you can meet customers where they are, offer help in the moment, and keep conversations consistent across every channel. Here’s how it can work: Web chat: A shopper browsing your site gets a product recommendation from Customer Agent. For example, they receive a recommendation for a pair of running shorts based on their past purchases or preferences. They add the item to their cart, but don’t check out. Instead of losing that interaction, the conversation data feeds into Klaviyo, ready to trigger the next step. SMS: Later, that same shopper receives an SMS abandoned cart flow. The message invites them to reply if they have questions about the product. They respond with: “What shorts are best for running marathons?” Customer Agent instantly provides a tailored, conversational answer, complete with a link to the right product. This time, they complete the purchase, no human agent needed. Email: After checkout, the shopper receives an order confirmation and later an email saying their package is out for delivery. When they reply to ask, “Where’s my order?” Customer Agent immediately retrieves tracking details and confirms the order is arriving today. The shopper gets peace of mind, and your support team never has to handle the repetitive inquiry. The bottom line: By placing Customer Agent across web chat, SMS, and email, you create a connected, self-service experience that scales effortlessly during peak BFCM volume. It’s like extending your team’s capacity without hiring seasonal help—keeping your customers supported, engaged, and ready to buy again. 3. Nudge people toward completing their purchase with an AI shopping assistant Slow response times are a top pain point during BFCM. Our AI consumer shopping survey found that 75% of consumers have abandoned an online purchase because they couldn’t find quick product answers. And according to the Baymard Institute , one of the reasons people abandon their carts is that the check-out process is too long or complicated. During BFCM, when people are making quick decisions, a small nudge from a customer data-informed AI agent may be exactly what you need to have a better Q4 than you did last year. Customer Agent can smooth out the check-out process by providing quick answers to common product questions, increasing the likelihood that someone will complete their purchase. Customer Agent keeps shoppers engaged and tackles conversion obstacles with: Real-time responses to frequent customer inquiries, such as sizing, shipping timelines, etc. “Add to cart” prompts within conversations Conversational help for customers who are browsing When you upload brand-specific collateral (PDFs, documents, guides), Customer Agent learns from these materials to offer shoppers custom responses and recommendations. And as it chats with customers and learns more about them, it gets even better at offering personalized service. The bottom line: During BFCM, when shoppers are pulled in all directions by attention-grabbing promotions from competitors, an AI shopping assistant can offer quick answers that lead to faster purchase decisions when there’s hesitation. 4.
